html:
The Battle of Hampton Roads was fought on 8 and 9 March 1862 in Hampton Roads, a harbour at the mouth of the James River in Virginia, United States. On its second day two ironclad warships fought each other for the first time: the Confederate CSS Virginia and the Union USS Monitor. Neither could sink the other.

In the American Civil War the Union navy blockaded the ports of the Confederacy. To break the blockade, the Confederates rebuilt a captured steam frigate, the Merrimack, with sloping iron armour and renamed it Virginia. On 8 March it steamed out, rammed and sank one wooden warship and burned another. Their shots bounced off its sides. About 240 Union sailors died. That night the Monitor arrived from New York. It was small and low, with two heavy guns in a turning turret. On 9 March the two ships fired at each other at close range for about four hours and did little damage. Both then pulled away.

The blockade held. But the fight showed that wooden warships were finished. Navies around the world, led by the Royal Navy, turned to iron ships with guns in turrets.
